source.version: Web application without a public build: record the capture date, the account type (personal or Workspace, never the address) and the page format
source.copyBrowser: Copy in Google Docs and paste in the same browser: Google Docs writes the clipboard from inside the page, so each browser is its own source path

editor.adapt: The same address with formatting=adapt. A scenario with an editorQuery adds it to both addresses.
editor.images: No allowRemoteImages and no imageAssets. Chrome's captures hold every image as a data:image/png URL in the HTML, with its alt text and size, and no file: the editor keeps it as an embedded image, quietly. A destination that refuses data images, or has no image node, removes it with image-removed, its alt text staying in its place. An image Google Docs served by URL would be removed the same way; none of the captured copies holds one
editor.lineHeight: Google Docs writes a block's line spacing as a CSS line height of 1.2 times it, so its default 1.15 is 1.38 on every paragraph, heading and list item, and a table cell's default, single, is 1.2. Cleanup reads the Docs spacing back and drops those defaults as the document's own, so the default schema without LineHeight reports only a spacing of its own, as GB19's 1.5, with destination-formatting-unconfirmed
editor.lineBreaks: Google Docs writes an empty paragraph as a br between blocks: two for two empty paragraphs, one before each table, one between two lists and one for the last paragraph after a final table. Cleanup makes each the empty paragraph it stands for, which the scenarios name
editor.correction: Corrected after the Chrome captures of 2026-10-05: images were expected as URLs and removed, line spacing as unconfirmed on every paragraph, and the breaks as unnamed blocks

conventions: This is an offline edited English regression specification. Block IDs and v1 document names remain stable. No native recapture was performed; baseline application instructions describe the shape being modeled.
Every paragraph starts with its block identifier, so any output order, loss or duplication is visible.

Create each document as a new Google Docs document with the title given here. Never create one by uploading or importing a .docx, .odt or .html file: that would capture a third party conversion. The large document is the one exception, pasted from a local browser tab as its blocks describe.

Before entering text, turn off Tools > Preferences > Automatically capitalize words, Use smart quotes and Automatic substitution. Copy each text from this file and paste it with Paste without formatting (Cmd+Shift+V), then apply the formatting named in docs.
A marker in list.docsLabel is what Google Docs shows. Do not type it; Google Docs creates it from the list formatting.

Images come from content/google-docs-images.mjs. Insert them only with Insert > Image > Upload from computer, never by URL, from Drive, Photos or a search, and give each the alt text named here (Cmd+Option+Y).
Keep the defaults of a new document: Pages format, Normal text in Arial 11 pt. Add no comments, suggestions, people, smart chips, bookmarks or headers.
Copy and paste in the same browser, and record the scenario's selection exactly.

A document's textStyle is the text style of Google Docs' Normal text as Docs shows it, Arial 11 pt, and a block's textStyle that of its own style, such as a heading's size and color; Docs' default black is no color. A pasted run may keep these values or none, never another. With them the comparison is exhaustive, as for Word: a block, an empty paragraph, a mark or a style the specification does not author for a selection is a finding. The large image, mixed and large documents are not captured and author none.
Corrections after the first captures say what changed and why in a correction field on the block or scenario; the earlier expectation is not kept.

The Google Docs fonts and sizes stay as text styles (GB04 in Arial 11 pt, the headings in Arial 20, 16 and 14 pt) and Heading 3 keeps its gray #434343; black, Docs' default text color, is no color of the runs. Paragraph spacing and Docs' default line spacing are the document's own and dropped without a finding.

Google Docs draws each script as a span of 0.6em aligned to sub or super inside its run: that size is how Docs draws a script, which the subscript and superscript marks draw in the destination, so the 2 keeps its run's 11 pt. The default schema has neither mark, so there the 2 pastes plain and destination-formatting-unconfirmed shows the notice in both policies.
